items.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: I made a recording of it with Dizzy Gillespie and Sonny Rollins back around 1958

ctx.x: So you were listening to a large ensemble and bringing it down to the piano.

Well the piano was featured in the orchestra. It was a feature piano thing. Actually it was like a trio recording right up until the very end of the tune, then the band comes in on the last chorus and plays a little riff behind the piano, and so it was basically a piano recording within the band, the Erskine Hawkins Orchestra. I really, really love this tune, and I finally, all my life it was a dream of mine to play this song with Erskine Hawkins, because you know I made a recording of it with Dizzy Gillespie and…

of playing it better than Avery Parrish, which I never believed, never, not for a minute. So anyway, I was on a boat cruise, on a jazz cruise once and Erskine Hawkins’ band was on the cruise also, and I met Mr. Hawkins and I just came out and asked him, I said, “Mr. Hawkins, I learned ‘After Hours’” — he knew who I was, he knew that I wasn’t just anybody, he knew that I could play — I said, “Could I come in and play this tune with the band one night?” He says, “Sure, come by tonight around ten o’clock and let me…
